Title: User successfully accesses the application from the updated allowed origin (no-q.club) without CORS errors
Preconditions: User has a valid session and the application is deployed with the updated CORS configuration
Steps:
1. Open a web browser and navigate to the application URL (e.g., https://no-q.club). 2. Log in to the application using valid credentials. 3. Navigate to any functional area (e.g., Appointment Reservation, Worker Management). 4. Perform a standard action (e.g., create an appointment, add a worker). 5. Verify the action completes without errors or CORS-related warnings in the browser console.

Test Data: User credentials: username='testuser', password='validpassword'; Appointment details: customerName='John Doe', customerPhone='1234567890', serviceItem='Haircut', date='2024-12-25', time='10:00 AM'
Expected Result: The application loads successfully. All API calls complete without CORS-related errors. The user can perform actions (e.g., create an appointment, add a worker) and view data as expected without any access issues.

Title: Attempt to access API from an unauthorized origin (non-whitelisted domain)
Preconditions: User is logged into the application and has a valid session. The application is running and accessible via a web browser.
Steps:
1. Open the browser's developer tools (F12).
2. Navigate to the 'Network' tab.
3. In the browser address bar, enter a direct API endpoint URL (e.g., the shop management API).
4. Manually modify the 'Origin' header in the request to a non-whitelisted domain (e.g., 'https://unauthorized-site.com').
5. Send the request.

Test Data: Origin: https://unauthorized-site.com
Expected Result: The browser should block the request due to CORS policy. The API should not return any data, and the browser's console should display an error message indicating that the request was blocked by CORS policy (e.g., 'Access to fetch at [API URL] from origin [unauthorized-site.com] has been blocked by CORS policy').

Preconditions: User is logged into the application and has a valid session with credentials (e.g., cookies or tokens). The application is running and accessible via a web browser.

5. Ensure the 'withCredentials' flag is set to true (or cookies are included).
6. Send the request.

Test Data: Origin: https://unauthorized-site.com, withCredentials: true
Expected Result: The browser should block the request due to CORS policy. The API should not return any data, and the browser's console should display an error message indicating that the request was blocked by CORS policy (e.g., 'Credentials is not supported if the CORS header ‘Access-Control-Allow-Origin’ is *').

Title: Verify that CORS policy restricts API access to the updated allowed origin only
Preconditions: 1. The application is running and accessible. 2. A test environment is available with the updated CORS configuration (allowed origin: https://no-q.club). 3. A disallowed origin (e.g., https://malicious-site.com) is available for testing.
Steps:
1. Open a browser or API client (e.g., Postman). 2. Configure the request to target any API endpoint (e.g., appointment reservation retrieval). 3. Set the 'Origin' header to 'https://no-q.club'. 4. Send the request. 5. Observe the response headers. 6. Repeat steps 2-5 with the 'Origin' header set to 'https://malicious-site.com'.

Test Data: 1. Allowed origin: https://no-q.club. 2. Disallowed origin: https://malicious-site.com. 3. API endpoint: /api/appointments (or any other endpoint).
Expected Result: 1. For the allowed origin (https://no-q.club), the response includes the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header with the value 'https://no-q.club' and the 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials' header with the value 'true'. The request succeeds with HTTP status 200 OK. 2. For the disallowed origin (https://malicious-site.com), the response does NOT include the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header with the disallowed origin, or the request fails with HTTP status 403 Forbidden or CORS error.
